utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, General. Yesterday, we went through a number of documents in an accelerated manner. I assume that we can continue the same way in this stage too. What is the content of the order on the engagement of forces in destroying Siptar terrorist groups in the broader area of Tusus that you adopted on the 14th of May 1999, and which is contained in tab 562?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an order, a classical one, if I can put it that way. Excuse me, could the map please be placed on the ELMO? Excuse me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: The map that is contained in document 563 should be placed on the easel, the one that pertains to this particular engagement of forces. So the order is in document 562, and the map is in 563. Is that right, General?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right, Mr. Milosevic. In paragraph 1 of this order, in the first three lines we can practically see the reason for engaging the forces. "From the beginning of aggressor NATO aviation's aggression against our country a group of Siptar terrorists are constantly operating from the Tusus sector locates around 15 to 20 terrorists, as printed. The Siptar terrorist group headquarters in Tusus is intensively carrying out a forceful mobilisation of the Siptar population from the neighbouring villages."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please be asked to slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic and the general, you just heard the interpreters asking you to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the town of Prizren. Tusus is a suburb, basically, of Prizren. From the beginning of the aggression up to that particular day on this road that leads from the village of Hoca Zagradska via the village of Leskovac to Prizren, about ten members of my unit got killed, as well as MUP members. These were columns that were bringing supplies, and all these attacks were carried out by this group of terrorists. And in order to neutralise this group of terrorists, this combat action was carried out and the order pertains to that combat action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just clarify this. Your supplies columns are moving there in the vicinity of Prizren. Ten men got killed in these attacks and you are now intervening vis-a-vis the group that did that. That is the content of this order.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: I would like to draw your attention to 8.5 of your order. You say: "In all situations, consistently honour the provisions of international law of war." That is, after all, contained in every one of your orders.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In every one of my orders, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. You've explained the map. In document 564, in accordance with the same procedure that was seen in other situations whenever the army was engaged, you wrote an analysis?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a detailed analysis of this particular action.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In this analysis we see what your estimate is; namely, that four persons were killed.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We assume that they got two more out. Our forces had three men killed and two wounded, whereas the MUP had two policemen killed and one wounded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is written here at the beginning of the last third of this analysis. That is the entirety of this particular engagement in this stage. Now, General, if you agree, if there is no special reason for us to dwell on these tabs, in the meantime I wanted us to look at tab 574.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I would just like to read one sentence from tab 566.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intelligence information that is sent from the brigade to the 2nd Motorised Battalion in Djakovica. "On the basis of information collected by intelligence and reconnaissance organs in the border zone ... "A movement of the Albanian army forward defence line and the allied forces on the border was carried out along the axis from the Republic of Albania to Kosovo and Metohija, with populated places as support points, between three and five kilometres in depth;. "In the sector of the Kosare border post, they committed aggression against the FRY territory ..." and I'm asking for particular vigilance because the aggression may start any day. That is what I wish to say about this particular tab.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Then there was a massive attack on our territory that you managed to repel successfully. That's what you talked about yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I can't actually find that quotation. I saw part of it but the bit about every day I couldn't find, or I missed it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Can you point us to the particular section, Mr. Milosevic or the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's a very short document, 566, the one that was just quoted by General Delic now. At the very beginning, in line four of the text, it says: "A movement of the Albanian army and allied forces on the border was carried out along the axis from the Republic of Albania to Kosovo and Metohija, with populated places as support points, between three and five kilometres in depth." And then: "In the sector of the Kosare border post, they committed aggression against the FRY territory."

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: It may be at line 4.12 that what sounded like quotation was a change from recitation to narration by the witness, but that's the problem with going at this sort of speed on passages that he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just briefly deal with document 574. If you have something that is exceptionally important in these documents that we are skipping, please draw my attention to that, General. So document 574. What does it pertain to? Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic. That is a document or, rather, an order in view of what was obtained in the previous document, this is an order consisting of eight paragraphs to subordinate units to carry out all preparations for organising battle, combat action, and every other tactical operation, to set up firing systems and coordinate them with the barrier systems, and ensure and facilitate effective attacks on enemy forces in the foreground at the combat support position in front of the forward line as well as in-depth defence during combat. Also ensure that each individual knows his place and that of his unit in the combat disposition of a higher-ranking unit of the last detail, et cetera. That is the essence of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In all possible aspects it has to do with the defence of the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, let us look at document 580. This is a warning that has to do with crime control in units, and I just wish to quote part of it. The third subparagraph in terms of what individuals do, as you say. That is: "Violent behaviour manifested so far in threats with weapons, random shooting at residential buildings, physical and sexual abuse, harassment." And then you give an example, too. So you constantly bear in mind what is going on in practice, and you caution that measures should be taken in order to eradicate this by all means. Is that the essence of this order of yours?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is the essence, because orders are received from superior commands and then one draws on all this experience preventing such things from happening in one's own unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That's precisely what I wanted to say. You indicate the example of another brigade, and you inform your own unit about this. So although such a thing did not happen in your unit, you're telling them that that kind of thing should not happen, should not be repeated or, rather, not repeated but never happen.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well, General. Now, in document 589 there's a criminal report regarding terrorism, and here we have an individual example of a KLA member who claims that he fled from the KLA and was captured bearing arms, with weapons on him, and how he has treated. Was he treated in the proper manner as prescribed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you said 589 tab, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. No, I apologise. No. I meant 583.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember this particular case. It took place on the 22nd of May. It is indeed a criminal report against an individual, and that individual was linked up to the operations of the 17th of May and the events that took place there. And in the close vicinity of the unit, in the town itself where the logistics unit was located, he appeared armed, wearing a black uniform. And when the person encountered the security forces, it was night-time, they threw away their rifle. They were arrested, and the person was treated pursuant to the rules.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this was an individual member of the KLA that was found wearing a black uniform, an automatic rifle, and everything else that it says here. You have his statement, you have the statement of your men from your unit, and we can see that this took place on the 22nd of May - that is the date of the document - that is to say, two months after the start of the NATO aggression. And this is an individual case. Is this, then, an example of conduct and proceedings with an arrested member of the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Proceedings were taken. He was taken to a military court, put before a military court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Now, if I omit something that you consider to be very important, please stop me, but I'm doing my best to use my time as best as possible. And I'd now like to ask you to take a look at the following document, which is tab 589. Let's see what that one's about.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is once again a military recruit and a criminal report against him. It is a person from my unit based in Djakovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, here we can see, among other things -- we're not going to go through this particular criminal report and what happened because it's a document that everybody can read, all of us can read through it, but I would just like to point out that we can see here that the citizens who were mistreated and abused reported the incident to the military police.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And the military police intervened. The perpetrator was arrested, a criminal report was filed, and medical assistance given to the injured parties.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All the reports were collected, from the Official Note of MUP, the Official Note by the security organs, the statements of all persons involved, and a photo documentation about the event, and this person was court-martialed forthwith.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, you also drew up a piece of information which is, in fact, the next document, about some crimes and negative events, and the date of that is the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: It is to be found in tab 590.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And in that piece of information we focus on the previous case in particular, the one we discussed a moment ago, that is to say the particular individual we discussed. And this was information sent out to all units, all the forces, so that all the members of the brigade could become acquainted with the case. The report briefly goes through what happened. Their attention is drawn to the fact that this was the perpetration of a crime under Article 3 of the Criminal Code of Serbia, that it was perpetrated in a demeaning manner and a brutal manner and that the sentence for crimes of that kind ranges between 3 and 15 [Realtime transcript read in error "4"] years in prison for the perpetrator, and for anybody else present and involved in aiding and abetting, they too will be held responsible and they will suffer the same sentence as in the previous case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And here it is noted that these persons were arrested by the military police and handed over to the military court in Pristina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And at the end of this report, all the commanders and leaders are required energetically to stop such acts from taking place. So you have a concrete event and you are informing all the members, all the men, that is to say several thousand men, members of your brigade, your forces, and at that time, at the time of you doing so, the perpetrators had already been arrested. Is that what we can learn from this document, deduce and conclude?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the substance of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, what was the range of possible sentences that you gave?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lowest sentence was 3 years -- 3 to 15 years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I thought so. The transcript says 3 to 4 years.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The general did say that in the report the sentence provided for by law range between 3 and 15 years.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, in the intelligence report by Colonel Vladimir Stojiljkovic, dated the 4th of June, mention is made among other things that at a border crossing there were cases that took -- there were events that took place --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Tab number, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's tab 595.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, please, General, would you tell us what that was about, what was happening.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date was the 4th of June, and that was already the time when the greatest ground offensive was under way, and its name was Arrow from -- coming from Albanian territory into the territory of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. And in that offensive we had taking part on the one side the terrorist forces, the forces of the Republic of Albania, and the NATO forces on the one side; and on the other side you had our own army, and this is intelligence, an intelligence report where the Chief of Staff, through his organs, defined and set out the four basic axes of attack via Pastrik -- Mount Pastrik. Otherwise, the operation was launched on the 27th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, do you claim that at any stage NATO forces actually entered the territory of Yugoslavia from the ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] NATO forces supported and reinforced, both from the ground and especially from the air, the forces of the terrorists who were attacking and who entered the territory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you answer my question. Do you say that the NATO forces at any stage entered the territory of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did not enter directly. NATO forces did not enter directly. The terrorist forces did enter, and they were supported and reinforced by NATO forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: General Delic, could you locate the location of Mount Pastrik on that map, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Pastrik. Mount Pastrik is here, to the west of Prizren. This is the valley of the Drim River. Here we have Vrbnik lake, and this is Pastrik mountain. This is the peak. It is 1.998 metres above sea level. And this ranged from the top, from the watchtower of Lika to Vrbnik lake. And that was the front. It ranged a distance of ten kilometres, and that's where the Operation Arrow started from Albania. The object was to reach the valley as soon as possible, the Beli Drim River valley, and to take control of Prizren as soon as possible. And the BBC, CNN reported on this constantly. There were constant news reports. And on the 30th or 31st of May, even, they informed the public that the forces had already reached the Drim valley, Drim River valley, and that on that day our army suffered 700 casualties. That is to say, they destroyed a battalion of 700 men.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: In connection to Mr. Bonomy's question as to whether the NATO forces actually entered the territory, the forces that were attacking the border were part of the overall forces which were supported by NATO, and they were the forces of the Republic of Albania, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Indeed. It's so hopeless to approach the examination of a witness in chief in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Whose planes were the B52 fighters who bombed all your positions simultaneously? Whose planes were they?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were US planes, B52s, and they took off from Great Britain.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This activity, the bombing of your positions at the same time as this attack was being launched, was that a unified activity that was being carried out on our territory?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the viewpoint of the deployment of strategic aviation, of a strategic air force, that is to say strategic planes were used to target tactical targets, and there was blanket bombing, as it's called, that is to say 20 -- carpet bombing. Twenty times between the 27th of May to the 8 was carpet bombing took place on the part of strategic B52 bombers. They bombed 25 times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And was this this united attack on our territory, including the ground aggression that was going on at the same time?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. This was direct support and reinforcement to terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: And of course to the forces of the Republic of Albania?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the forces of the Republic of Albania who used their own artillery, their own tanks, and everything else they had at their disposal - artillery divisions - to act against our forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Two points, General, just -- as you will appreciate -- thank you for that further information, but as you will appreciate, my question was a very simple question about who actually penetrated on the ground, and now we've had clarification of certain other aspects which doesn't add to the answer you've already given. The other matter I want to ask you is this: You referred to news reports of 700 casualties. Are you saying these are inaccurate news reports?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The figure is incorrect. It is true that in one day, on one day from my unit 125 people were out of combat. Of that number, ten were killed and 115 wounded, but they were placed out of action, they were not able to take part in the fighting any more. But together with the bombing of these positions and in all that together, I think 28 people were killed. So the information, the piece of news that 700 people were killed is not correct, in a single day. That was not the right figure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I think you were also saying that the report was inaccurate in relation to the amount of progress that the forces had made. That's the invading forces.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. And our radio television, Radio-Television Serbia, that is, filmed the spot, the watchtower at Gorozur, and showed the whole world that that piece of information put out by CNN was completely incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. That was a surprise because CNN -- that was a surprise, I suppose, because CNN is well known for its correct Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. information, is it not? General --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is that a question or a comment? Because if it's a question, we have haven't got the answer yet. Do you have an answer to that question, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that Mr. Jamie Shea, as the "portparole" of NATO, celebrated the NATO pact during the aggression against our country and the whole world was able to hear his reports, which were full of lies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, you've now described the situation. We have a ground operation going on, strategic planes bombing our forces in the area in depth, away from the border into Yugoslavia, and now in document 607, for example, your organs of the military police, your -- of your Prizren garrison, were filing a criminal report, and we see the date there. It is the 5th of June, that is to say the period of time when the worst attacks were being launched precisely against your units, and in your unit -- yet in your unit a criminal report was being filed on that particular date, the 5th of June, against a perpetrator who was killing and wounding an enemy contrary to the Criminal Code and Article 146 of that Criminal Code.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this was a member of your unit involved.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Do you happen to know, in view of the fact that you are a teacher, a professor and a military man yourself, that this level of efficiency for organs when they are engaged in high level operations, very difficult operations, were they efficient in filing that criminal report?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were, because the -- in these very difficult times it was their duty not to allow any unlawful acts from being committed. No defeatism, no panic. And so in this particular case, they were very efficient in taking steps to stop the perpetrators, and in this case it was one of their members. So they arrested one of their own men.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: They arrested a member of the military police who had killed an Albanian; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What happened to him, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it says here in this criminal report. Now, as far as the soldier is concerned, the soldier was arrested straight away.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, it's him -- it's what happened to the soldier is what I would like to know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The soldier was taken into custody and court-martialed straight away, sent to the military court in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what happened at the military court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the following tabs, you will find that. We can see -- actually, it's in tab 626.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just tell me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In tab 626, as I said, we find that the proceedings were undertaken. The court undertook the appropriate proceedings, but I have to find this particular individual now in the files. Slavoljub Topalovic was his name, soldier. The case was handed over to the municipal public prosecutor in Prizren.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And what happened there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. It was a civil court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This is one of a number of occasions we've run into this difficulty, that we get so far in the -- in the account of what happened in relation to something, and then we end up up a close, as we say, up a side street that leads to a dead end. Anyway, if you don't have the information, we'll no doubt hear from someone else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That accords with the view expressed by Mr. Milosevic, that the responsibility under Article 7(3) ends with arrest, and that is certainly not the case. The question of punishment also arises, which means that the trial is important, what happened at the trial is significant. But consistently you don't provide information beyond arrest. Proceed, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we look at this tab, it shows also the sentences meted out to the members of my unit.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, if it is necessary to follow through all the cases that were processed further up the line, it's possible, but I thought it would be rational for me to deal with that. The constitution of Yugoslavia and the constitution of Serbia very clearly stipulate, as in every democratic country, a distribution of power between executive, legislative, and judiciary authorities, and the executive authorities have finished their job when they refer a case to the judiciary. I am not saying by any means that the judiciary did not perform their functions. I'm certain they did, and people who committed crimes were convicted. And we can also get hold of that information as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Never mind what the constitutional position is in your country. Criminal responsibility under Article 7(3) relates both to the prevention and punishment of crime, which means that the trial is also important. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I personally am not aware of a single case where somebody who perpetrated a crime and was convicted would have been released or acquitted. But we will look into that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you're not giving evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let us just have a look here. There are a couple of additional things that relate to -- could you please look at the document under 616. My copy is very poor. What is this all about?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report under tab 616, saying that the activities of Siptar terrorist forces are being intensified, as well as the activities of the NATO aviation, so that from 6.00 to -- 6.00 a.m. [as interpreted] to 8.00 p.m., aviation acted against Planeja village, Sinaj, and towards the top of the mountain Pastrik, with frequent use of cluster bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: This is an intelligence report that in fact corroborates what you just said about the ground invasion and the use of strategic aviation against our forces at the time.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And those three villages that I mentioned were completely destroyed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: But I understood that the carpet bombing covered the entire area of these villages where our forces were located.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Carpet bombing implies that an entire territory is constantly bombed with aircraft acting in pairs, and each plane carries around 50 225-kilo bombs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, General. Could we now look at another document, which is an excerpt from an annual intelligence report on electronic surveillance and counter-electronic operations for 1999. It's under tab 618. Could you please point out the highlights, the most important points made in this document. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have. For instance, on page 43 [as interpreted], the beginning of that page, this is actually a report received by Siptar terrorist forces via radio, namely an order that on the 3rd of March, beginning with 8.00 a.m., they should be in the highest level of combat readiness, take up their positions, and be in constant mutual contact. At 2300 hours, the Siptar terrorist forces located in this area --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My mistake, no doubt -- oh, yes, I've found it now. Top of the page 3. There's a reference to page 43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You previously took objection to a similar document, Mr. Nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have taken objection to this sort of document. I'm not sure what the ruling was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: The reason I'm interested in is that it was a majority ruling at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take the same objection, of course, to documents of this kind because the raw material won't be made available to us, unless the witness has brought it with him, and I'm unable, therefore, to deal with it at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It also doesn't indicate exactly what it is. It's an incomplete document and one which the -- it's not clear that the general has direct knowledge of, or one which contains material of which he has direct knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I certainly repeat my objection, and I'll take the matter further in cross-examination, if I have time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So, General, you read from their report on electronic surveillance and listening in to enemy communications.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the 52nd Company for electronic surveillance of the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Can we find something here that was not directly overheard during their work of listening in to enemy communications?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. This is an annual report, the report for 1999. Last year we discussed another annual report for 1998, and from that report we received this extract that relates to terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. So this is the beginning of March, dealing with terrorist activities. Look at the entry for the 14th of May: "By intercepting Siptar terrorist radio communications for the Pastrik operation zone at 0200 hours on 14 May, 1999, we found out --"

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speaker please slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "... we found out that NATO aviation dropped cluster bombs along the axis of Dulje village --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The interpreters are asking you to slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will slow down.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: "-- Blace village - Budakovo village - and Jezerske mountain, which resulted in a large number of dead and wounded refugees and Siptar terrorist forces members."

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is information received through interception.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So we see from these intercepts that they were discussing their own casualties resulting from NATO bombing.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It happened on the 14th of May. I mentioned it yesterday. In the night of the 13th, the heaviest bombing of Prizren happened, the heaviest for the entire war, and they were reporting their own losses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, can I take it that for that information the fact that for that information you refer to this document means that it wasn't intelligence which you reported on in any other form or incorporated into any order that you issued or analysis that you provided. This is, as far as your documents are concerned, the only source of this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There are many sources of intelligence. This is only one of them. It's not my unit but part of this unit located --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I haven't expressed that very well. This piece of intelligence here doesn't appear in any of the other documents you've referred us to. Does that mean that this intercepted information - and I confine the point to this piece of intercepted information - was something that you did not actually make use of at the time? It's not in any of your analyses or any of your orders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There was no need to. I used this information directly on the ground. If we take, for instance, this last specific information of the 14th of May, I had that information already. The bombing of the refugee column near Korisa happened around 8.00 p.m., twenty-five past eight. I had that information within minutes. And this report from this agency arrived only on the next day, so it was not relevant at the time, this specific piece of information, I mean. This is a unit of the superior command, so in my reports towards the superior command, there was no need for me to report to them what their own unit was doing and what kind of information it gave me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, indeed. That makes me wonder why on earth we're looking at this rather than your own personal experience of what actually happened on the ground, which is really what I'm interested in. What was the immediate source of your knowledge of the bombing of the refugee group?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, we dealt with it in detail yesterday, and we even watched video footage filmed by Radio-Television Serbia. So what we discussed yesterday and what we saw on the film, that same subject is discussed by terrorists via radio. It's the same event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But what I'm trying to understand is what was the first information you got that there had been -- that a group of refugees had been bombed? Who reported that to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received a report, of course, by my operations duty officer. I personally heard the sound of bombing, but I didn't know which area was being bombed, and my operations duty officer told me that it was the area of Korisa village. Because throughout the territory we had our units, but at that moment I didn't know that there were refugees there as well. I thought they were bombing an empty space because there were no units of mine there. And it was only around 3.00, 3.00 a.m., when the wounded started coming into the hospital, that I found out that there were casualties there, people killed, that the column of people on their way home had been hit. That's when I ordered my medical corps to be sent there to give assistance to these people. And my military hospital worked to take care of these wounded all the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: On the 28th of May we see another intercept. It says: "By intercepting Siptar terrorist radio communications we found out that they were setting up obstacles wherever they could and blew up roads used by our forces. The rest of their communications consisted of an exchange of short encoded notifications and open information related to the movement of our forces. We found out that from the Brestovac village - Samodreza village - Studencane line they control the movement of our forces along the Prizren-Orahovac and Prizren-Suva Reka axes, and that they are gathering their forces in the above-mentioned belt. "We found out that in the Kosare sector the Siptar terrorist forces have a lot of men wounded and killed and that they have been instructed to keep a low profile in the forthcoming period and not to carry out any attacks until they notice the movement of our forces." Now, what we see from these intercepts caught by this electronic surveillance company, does that coincide with the information you collected on the ground? That's my -- one question. And second, the information and reports you got from this company on a daily basis, in succession, although this was a company of your superior command, was it one of the sources of intelligence that you needed in order to make decisions on the ground?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, can I make it clear that that is the most blatant of leading questions, and really the answer to it is devalued as a result. Putting the answer to the witness and then asking the question is a pointless exercise in examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you continue to violate the rule against leading questions. You'll have to proceed to another question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. I did not think it was a leading question if I was quoting what was written in the report and if I asked the witness whether that corresponds with --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: When you formulate your questions in this double-barrelled manner, ending up with, "Was it one of the sources of intelligence that you needed in order to make decisions on the ground?" you are in effect telling the witness the answer. We have been through this many times. Proceed to ask another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, let's just have a look at the conclusion, at the end, from this document that has to do with electronic surveillance. Look at the conclusion. Look at what it says here.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the very end of all these reports, the company for electronic surveillance deals with the entire year, and it practically defines what the operation zones were that the terrorists mentioned, and they say here that it is six operation zones, that their division is not definite, and then that on the basis of their information they also have sub-zones. That by intercepting their communications, they practically identified 13 brigades of the KLA, that they assume they have a battalion system and their units are subdivided into companies and platoons. That is the conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When you say, General, they're dealing with the whole year, what do you mean by the "year"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The war period of 1999. I misspoke. I misspoke saying the entire year. It's from the beginning of 1999 until the end of the war.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Or is it until the 13th of June, which is the date immediately before the conclusion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, our units stayed on all the way up to the 26th of June. Although they were relocated from the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, it was only on the 26th of June that demobilisation was carried out of personnel from these units.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, could you please look at the general schematic. You mentioned what the conclusion was of this report and how the forces were organised of the KLA. Next page this same company gives a general scheme of the organisation, the Dragobilje staff, and then the operations zones.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: That can be seen on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that can be seen on the ELMO. This is a general scheme that was compiled by the 52nd Company in its analysis on the basis of its six-month work in 1999, what the operations zones are and what brigades are linked to which one of these zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. An integral part of these -- this document is a survey of found officers and forces in 1999. What does this document speak of? That document is contained in tab 619.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It speaks of the command structure of the KLA, which was confirmed through radio surveillance and radio goniometry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: With all their information?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Including when they were selected, who got killed where and when, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, all the information required.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: When was that compiled, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Like the report for 1998. As I said, it was compiled in January 1999. This report was compiled after the end of 1999, that is to say in January 2000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Who compiled it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was compiled by the commander of the 52nd Company for electronic surveillance, together with his officers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, since --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Tab 619 is part of the report which we were looking at in 618?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, an integral part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, when you say "annual report," you explained that annual reports are compiled in January for the preceding year. In the meantime, until the annual report is compiled, all this intelligence, as it is received, is it made available to you and to other command structures that may find them useful?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They would be pointless if they would not be sent on to the units that they pertain to momentarily in order to be of assistance, so they were sent on to the units immediately. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So at the end of the year there is only a compilation that is made which was in realtime sent to the units at the time when the information and intelligence was gathered. Is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is an analysis that is compiled at the end of the year that pertains to the overall activity for the previous year.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us deal briefly with this cooperation between NATO and the KLA. Was there intensive cooperation between NATO and the KLA?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was intensive cooperation, especially intensive --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... not in any expectation that there will be any response to an order of the Court that the accused should apply his mind to the rulings it's been making for a year or so, but that was a monstrous leading question and therefore it brings an answer of no value.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Nonetheless, I'm interested in the question of cooperation between NATO and the KLA, so I'd like the question to be answered. General, answer the question. Never mind the leading question by Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] During the war, there was incessant and two-way cooperation between the KLA and NATO. The KLA gave NATO intelligence as to the location of our forces. NATO used this information in preparing to bomb certain positions. On the other hand, NATO supported combat actions of the terrorist forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, when you say supported --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, is it any part of your case that any of the acts attributed to Serb forces, and therefore to you, as crimes in the indictment were committed in response to a combined attack by NATO and the KLA or NATO acting in concert with the KLA or the KLA acting in concert with NATO?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. Robinson. I hope that throughout the testimony of General Delic you were able to see each and every concrete situation; when there was movement of forces, when there was activity by our forces, and that in every concrete situation there -- this is actually a response to behaviour by the enemy, something the enemy did.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we need to be -- to be more specific. We have an indictment with charges, and I'm asking whether it is part of your case that any of the crimes that the indictment alleges were committed by you through your forces were committed in response to the KLA acting in concert with -- with NATO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would not put it that way, whether something was committed in response. What is certain is that a large number of KLA members were killed in clashes with our forces. There's no doubt about that. Since you're talking about the indictment, if you look at that, it's some kind of civilians that are referred to. Although they are on various lists and they're all men, but they are all claimed to be civilians. This is what they launched here through Mr. Nice, together with Mr. Nice; that our forces first shelled settlements, surrounded them, arrested, killed, which is a pure lie. You saw over a year and a half what it looked like -- what the movement of a big unit looked like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I didn't invite to you make a speech. It really is a question that has fundamental legal implications for the case, because if that is so, the nature of the conflict is changed. You have a group of states whom you say are acting with terrorist forces, and in my view, if you are responding to that attack, that implicates Article 51 of the United Nations Charter, and that's why -- that's the importance of that question, but proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that you put it right. It is self-defence, and that is the only thing that is allowed according to international law, use of force in self-defence. Our country fought against aggression.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the facts substantiate that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And how, Mr. Robinson. Nobody can deny these facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, let's look at some documents since I asked you about cooperation between NATO and the KLA. In tab 620, you have a list of discovered targets of the 4 -- of the 549th Brigade, your brigade. There is a map of these targets here too.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The map was something that my intelligence officer was in charge of. This is a survey of targets of my units, and the Siptar terrorists submitted this to NATO. That's about 35 to 40 targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: How did you get hold of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This was also received through radio intercepts when the observers of terrorists reported to their commands, which again had satellite telephones for communicating with NATO where different parts of my units were. I think this has been translated and that you can see this. That's the way in which these people operated, those who were observing, in view of their military knowledge, and they were informing on where which part of my unit was. And as soon as I learned about this, I moved my forces elsewhere so that they would not be threatened or jeopardised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Of course. From a military point of view, establishing a target and hitting a target, is this part of one and the same activity or are these independent activities?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is absolutely one and the same activity. In order to get to a target, there has to be information.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, when you use the word "support" of the NATO forces to the Siptar terrorists, are you referring to political support or are you talking about fire support, the use of air force, cruising missiles and so on and so forth? What are you referring to when you say "support"?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday and today I have primarily been speaking about this support that we call military support. That is to say fire support directly through means of combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: General, you distinguish between opportunism, that is the KLA taking advantage of the fact that there was NATO bombing, and coordination, the actual meeting or arrangement between NATO and KLA to act together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This arrangement was not made when the bombing started or during the course of the war. This arrangement was made considerably earlier. It is clear this is a Court of the United Nations. The aggression was not carried out with the permission of the United Nations. The UN was side-stepped by NATO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: General, that's not the question which Judge Bonomy asked. What he was seeking was whether -- seeking to find out whether you have specific evidence, more concrete evidence of coordination between NATO and the KLA, as distinct from mere speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's absolutely what I've been speaking about for the past two days. So there was a synchronised attack of terrorists somewhere in the territory, on the state border, and it was supported by NATO Air Force. Not only by B52s but also with A10 aircraft and other types of aircraft. There cannot be more tangible and specific cooperation than that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So what you're saying is, and it may be a perfectly reasonable proposition, I'm not being critical of it, I'm just trying to find out the facts that you're aware of, but what you're saying is that you draw the conclusion from the fact that these things happened simultaneously that they must have been deliberately coordinated. Now, I was really hoping that you would be able to be a bit more -- or to draw our attention to something more concrete as indicating direct agreement between them to act together.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And there are certainly things like that as well, but really, I don't know. You were thousands of kilometres away from the spot. For 78 days the bombing of my country went on. For 78 days there were synchronised attacks of NATO in concert with KLA operations.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, you saw on the video footage as well that Clark, the commander of NATO at the time, is called by the Albanians a KLA veteran. They themselves give him this kind of tribute.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So I emphasise, General, I understand the point you make entirely, but just so that we are clear about what the evidence -- there is no direct evidence that you're presenting to us of communications between NATO and the KLA in relation to coordinating their activities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely. Absolutely. We'll probably come across this in the next tabs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Now we'll come across the next tabs, but you have been testifying here for a few days now. General, we saw video footage of oath-taking, where reference is made to unification with Albania, and on the same day a meeting between the man who was reading out the oath with Holbrooke and his team as far as back as 1998. Did we not see that here on the videotape?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the first and second video that we saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So there is an alliance. Although before that they said it was a terrorist organisation, there is an alliance precisely with those who are proclaiming the secession of Kosovo and unification with Albania, at state level. Unprecedented. Do you think that that is evidence or not? General --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, I did not have the possibility of communicating with the general, however, apart from this tab 620 where we have a review of the targets and the map, I have received in the meantime a list of targets and information sent in to the 3rd Army during the war. So I would like the general to take a look at this now, this document which is very similar --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: This is not included in the tabs, what you're seeking now to present?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In tab 620, we do have one list of targets. However, in the meantime, as I say, I received a document of lists of targets and other information of electronic surveillance which was sent in to the 3rd Army of the Pristina Corps for the period ranging from the 6th of April to the 15th of June, as they came across them, and the general explained to us that this was done as quickly as possible. The units were sent in this information as speedily as possible to be able to move from the points and positions at which they were located as targets. And this was done in collaboration with NATO and the KLA throughout. The general can take a look at the document. It can be placed on the overhead projector. In the meantime, as I say, I received this document, and I consider that it would be very beneficial for us to see it and to hear the general's comments. I can hand it over to you straight away. That's tab 620 now. All right. Fine. We can discuss those targets as well. Could you hand this document over to the general.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Look at the title page, General, please, and the list itself, the structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Nothing has been said about where this document came from, apart from the fact that the accused says he got it. Unless the document in some way identifies its origin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'll ask the general. General, tell us about the origin, the source of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't we deal with 620 first and then let's come to that document later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, Judge Kwon is suggesting we deal with 620 first, since that's in the tab, and we'll follow that procedure.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. Yes, indeed. I think that the proposal is a very good one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, take a look at tab 620 now, please. You have it before you, you have it on the map, and you have a list there as well. Just take the targets one by one and tell us what this is about, because I can see you have the region, then you have the coordinates, then you have the units and the activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, deal with the provenance of the document first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: General, would you please be so kind as to tell us the provenance of this document. Where does this survey of discovered targets of the 549th Motorised Brigade come from?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As this is my brigade, this is a review of my intelligence officer, and this is a map compiled by my intelligence officer; and what it says here on this list and the coordinates given, he introduced those onto the map and placed numbers by these points. They were targets which were pinpointed, discovered, and sent out to NATO to be bombed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Are they exact targets as they were discovered and sent out to NATO to be bombed?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the first column, you have the region, the locations, the spots, and they are more or less accurate. Yes, it is accurate. My units were in those locations at that period of time. Now, in the other column, the coordinates are also accurate and correct. Now, the third column, the person who identified the units very frequently did not do this in detail, or he wasn't precise enough. But, yes, it is correct and accurate that when this was reported the army was there, the forces -- our forces were there. And I also said that upon learning this, our units, the units who were at these locations, at these coordinates, were moved. We moved them to other locations. And it was our assessment that what was needed was from the time this information was learnt to NATO bombing, that a space of about three to four days elapsed. So we had three to four days during which to act, because I assume that NATO with their surveillance planes would check out the information they were given by the KLA. So as soon as we heard this information, that they had learnt of our -- where our -- where we were, we were able to move our units from the general area, and so we did not suffer any losses thanks to this system that we put in place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. May we now take a look at the document that I received in the meantime, this additional document. Could you explain it to us, General. Have you ever seen this document before, anything like it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen this document before. It -- I am aware and acquainted with the document. It is in fact a report after the war of all the information and intelligence that came into us during the war at the time we learnt of them. The source here is the 280th Centre of Electronic Surveillance. It is the electronic surveillance centre attached to the air force and anti-air defence. And so the source of this information is communication between NATO planes with their command posts in the air. So it is surveillance plane communication and the AVAX [phoen], which were the command posts in the air or communication between the aircraft themselves, or communication between combat planes and planes for electronic jamming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at the ELMO, and could you comment, point this out to us.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This comprises several thousand pieces of information. So during one single day, if you look at any of these pages, you will see that Prizren is mentioned, for instance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So this gives us the dates, the coordinates, and all the targets. Tell us, please, General, in your assessment in the area of Kosovo and Metohija, how many projectiles were launched, were used? What would you say, during these 78 days of bombing?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the territory of Kosovo and Metohija, of course, is a large territory, but on my unit alone -- well, we looked at a tab where it says that on an average on a single day, about 100 projectiles were launched, on average.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there a difference between this as being a record of advance information and noting the locations where the attacks actually took place, or is it a combination of both or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is information -- it says here "Report." So according to the locations, not all of them, NATO was active. Now, these reports came in to us. You can see that each of the reports has the exact time noted - the hour, the minute, and perhaps even the second, I don't know - so when that piece of information was received. And that piece of information, through the operative on duty, was immediately sent out to the unit concerned, to the unit that was in jeopardy. There was a computer programme set up according to which when these data are introduced about the coordinates, the computer programme would straight away tell you where the point to be bombed was, where the target on the territory was, and the operations duty officer would immediately inform the unit concerned, the unit in -- that was threatened, the region where the NATO bombing was going to take place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What is the information in the right-hand column?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The information in the right-hand column are remarks. It says "Remarks." First of all you have the time, then the latitude, et cetera, and then the remarks, longitude and latitude, and then where the actual target is located within those coordinates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Remarks include references to -- well, they appear to include references to types of aircraft. If you could look at one of them. There's a word "Pozicija."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Pozicija," "position," B-52.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means where that particular plane is located at that point in time. When communication has been established with the air command centre, for example, if it is a fighter bomber or a bomber, when it has established contact with AVAX, it was at that position.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So that's information about what actually happened rather than advance information.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This is information which came in before something happened, because if you give information that a B-52 bomber was at such-and-such location in my area, that, for me, is a signal that I must tell my units and sound the alarm and that they should --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Help me a little more. Mr. Prendergast, can you move the ELMO out a little and you see there -- just a little further. These figures which precede the reference to "Pozicija B-52," what are these figures?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They are figures denoting the position. It is the geographic longitude and latitude at the point at which the plane is at the time it is reporting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... or is it in the air or what?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's all on the territory of our country.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it's in the air.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course in the air. An aircraft in the air. Hostile enemy aircraft in the air.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So it does reflect what actually happened, rather than advance information, which is what I asked you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's what is happening at that point in time in the air, and the consequence of that, what comes next, is the actual bombing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Without translation, it's very difficult to follow, so I would ask the general to take, for example, two or three lines and explain it to us in full after the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will do that after the break. We will adjourn for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: To use our time as rationally as possible and to put things very clearly, in keeping with the suggestions made by Mr. Kwon we looked at tab Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. 620 first.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Now, this electronic surveillance that we keep coming up against, in layman's terms does that mean interception, listening in, tapping in?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: So in tab 620, do we have what the KLA is reporting to NATO about your targets on the ground? Is that it?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's quite clear. It's what they are reporting about my unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Now, I already asked you this question, but this reporting and bombing, is it part of one and the same operation?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is the beginning and the end of one and the same operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Fine. Great. Now, you've provided us with a map about that. Now, as I've given you this long document, the big document with the times, the longitude and latitude, et cetera, I'd like to draw your attention to this: In tab 621, to all intents and purposes you have extracts from the document we've already provided. We didn't have the entire document at the time that I've handed over now, but tab 621 contains extracts, excerpts from that document.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I found it on the big document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now, since the long document hasn't been translated and as 621 has been translated, I'm going to draw your attention to the following: Look at tab 621 first, please. We have the title page first, and then it says NATO aggression against the FRY, and all the air forces are listed; how many British, American, French, Danish, Turkish, Dutch, Spanish, German, Italian, et cetera, aircraft. And then we have what I provided you with, that excerpt, on the following page of tab 621. That is what that shows. Now, take a look at, for example, number 1661, 1661 where are they issuing warnings. What does it say in the remarks?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "KLA zone warned that in a circle of three nautical miles they should not --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put the English version on the ELMO. That's the second page, 1661. Yes, that's it. Could we see the number. Yes. 1661. Time 2252, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. Then you have the longitude and latitude. I don't want to read that out. The degrees, then we have the minutes, the hours, et cetera. Then it says: "KLA zone warned not to be active in the area of three nautical miles. It is no-fly zone." So they should take care not to target their own forces.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And on that same page, higher up, this is mentioned twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: Yes, 1648 and 1649. "KLA active at 3 nautical miles from the centre of this point." And then at 1650, "KLA active at 3 nautical miles around this point." So what do these remarks actually mean?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are warnings to planes up in the air that at 3 nautical miles from that point all around, that they should not be active because that's where the KLA is located.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: All right, fine. Now take a look at the following page. I just have the last three or, rather, three numbers, three digits printed out. The first digit is missing, or the first two digits is missing, but it is nine lines from the top. 1930 -- from the bottom. 1933, where we have the longitude and latitude, and it says: "E-8 warned E-2C to call back the men from the target because the KLA members are there. This region is in the south-eastern quadrant of A-38." So, General, tell us, please, what does this data tell us and this evidence? What does it tell us?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This latest is an aircraft for electronic surveillance and they are warning that they're at the command centre to call back the planes back in that region so that they should not act against the terrorists.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Therefore, Mr. Robinson, what you say or, rather, the question you asked as to whether the army had perpetrated any crimes in order to react and respond to this, that that's not how it was. The army did not commit any crimes. That's the first point. The army, throughout the presentation of General Delic, performed activities and went into action to repel an unlawful attack simultaneously by NATO and the KLA. It was a simultaneous, unlawful attack on the part of NATO and the KLA together, and all the activities and movements of the army were to repel this simultaneous attack by NATO and KLA forces. I hope that's clear now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... repelling that attack the crimes in the indictment were committed? Is that your case? Because that is the only way that it becomes relevant.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is my opinion that it is not the case that crimes were committed. Those who were killed were killed in combat activities. Of course, war in itself is a crime, especially an aggression is, but defence and self-defence cannot be a crime. It is not us who attacked any NATO member country. NATO attacked us on our territory in coordinated action with the unlawful forces of the terrorists in that territory. I believe this is fundamental to the legal definition of what happened. A state has a legitimate right to defend itself from aggression and from terrorism. What we have here are terrorist forces and the NATO acting in league. That is completely clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, there's really no charge against NATO, and the NATO attack only becomes relevant if you can relate it in some way to the acts that are charged in the indictment, and the evidence will have to substantiate that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, you've produced a document in a table form, a tabular form, with these remarks on the right-hand side, and the general's giving evidence about his understanding of these remarks, and as far as I'm concerned this material could be of some importance in relation to the point you're making about coordination or joint activity between NATO and the KLA, but as I've indicated before when you referred to the annual report of the surveillance information obtained, I find the form in which it's presented very unsatisfactory. There must be something better to substantiate these remarks which the witness is endeavouring to interpret for us. There must be the notes that were originally made from which this record has been compiled. There must be a better basis. And you yourself surely -- you yourself must appreciate that this sort of compilation, which is obviously open to interpretation, which relies on a summary being put together, is an unsatisfactory way of dealing with something as important as this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Bonomy, this is not a compilation. This is an agglomerated, comprehensive report, an agglomeration of all reports that were made throughout the year in realtime and the conclusions drawn from them in realtime. So the annual report only gathers all the information in one place, all the intercepts that were made throughout the year through electronic surveillance.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: But some of the remarks are comments that are said to have been overheard and recorded, and you've just led some evidence about these, but there are other remarks here which could be anything. You know, if says "target 10.4 kilometres south-east of Prizren," that could be anything. It doesn't give us any real indication of the source of that information, and it certainly would be helpful to me if at some stage you were able to demonstrate what was behind some of the important remarks that are made in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Can I just raise a matter in relation to Judge Robinson's question to the accused, because there is an issue here which hasn't been raised by the accused this morning but it's something that I raised yesterday and on several previous occasions. He's charged with the crimes of forcible transfer and deportation, and all those events, as you'll see from the indictment, are on the 25th of March onwards, largely from that date onwards. The combined activities of the KLA and NATO delivering, as the general said in his area, 100 bombs a day, that activity leads to the force -- leads to the transfer, the migration, if you like, leads to the forcible transfer issue in this case. Is it migration? Is it forcible transfer? And the people leaving, uprising almost, if you like, from the state of Kosovo, from the -- not the state of Kosovo, from the Kosovo region, the territory, the migration of those people in relation to the response of the KLA and NATO is very important in relation to Defence issues in this trial.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Kay. So that's another -- that's another area in which the NATO attack is related to the charges.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And consistently the accused has put that element in his case. He hasn't mentioned it today, but it is something that's been a material feature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And we've had some evidence of that from witnesses? Through the general, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. KAY
utterances.text: Yes. And from other witnesses. It's been a consistent thread.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
