utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, for today's evidence, did you proceed by way of groups?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Partially today, too, because I received your approval yesterday to go through April and May documents as a group. So we just flew through these documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I suppose until the end of April and May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The tabs.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot see that now. I cannot find that paper, but it was somewhere up to 610 or maybe 612. Let me just see. I went through -- specifically through 607, the criminal report that we've seen. That's the beginning of June. Certainly all the way until 600, and then I went individually through the most important documents all the way to the end. I dealt with them one by one together with the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. We'll give a ruling on the admission of the remaining documents on Monday. In the meantime, Mr. Nice, you may start.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: I only have time for a couple of details. Just dealing with Lord Ashdown, can I have a copy of that map, please. And the second thing is, the map you've been referring to as marked by the Prosecution is in fact a map that was handed to you blank, like this, you marked in it yourself the proposed position of Lord Ashdown, and then you marked in the shading in red; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But you have to know that you provided me with an unacceptable map, totally inadequate to such precise work.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Please make such comments if you think they're going to be helpful. We actually provided you with two maps, one too detailed; you asked for another one, we provided you this one, the best we could find, you marked it, we sent it to Lord Ashdown, and I'd now like a copy of the map you've got and we'll send that to him as well. So if I can have that, please. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Right, let's just deal in the remaining time with one topic. Where were you stationed in 1989?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 1999 and 1998 I was stationed in Prizren. That's what -- where my --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Prizren. That's where my command was. In 1999.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1989, I was in Belgrade, of course.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1990, also in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In 1991, where were you based then?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of the time from 1987 until 1995 I was working at the military academy in Belgrade, except for the fact that in certain periods, such as in 1991 and 1992 and another period in 1993-1994, I was on the battlefield, once in Croatia and another time in Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Precisely. In 1991, you were on the battlefield in Croatia. Whereabouts; at Dubrovnik?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not in Dubrovnik itself but in the surrounding area.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Oh, really? Which part of the surrounding area?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the location of the command for civilian affairs, called Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: And you indeed appeared at the Cavtat talks, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: 1992, what part of the battlefield, if any, did you appear on in 1992?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1992, that was that period. I was responsible for civilian affairs at the command for civilian affairs, as I said, which was based in Cavtat.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: In Cavtat. Very well. In 1993?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1993, until April, I was working at the military academy in Belgrade, and from April until September I was in Bosnia-Herzegovina around Ljubinje.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes. What was your -- what was your role there?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean 1993?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: For a month I was Chief of Staff of the 715th Brigade, and after that I was the officer for intelligence and security.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1994, I was working at the military academy.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: You didn't leave Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the 6th of February, 1995, onwards, I was in Prizren occupying the position of Chief of Staff until the 26th of July, when I became commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Are you saying you stayed in Kosovo, so far as duty is concerned, from that time onwards?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From that time onwards I was in the 549th Motorised Brigade, apart from the period that I spent in training. But throughout that time I continued to occupy my position in the brigade. From the 2nd of September until the 26th of July, 1997, I was at the school for national defence in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: One last question because I suspect it's time that we have to rise unless we --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Another two minutes, until a quarter to.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: About 20 minutes ago you gave a very long answer about the Joint Command, something that you had been questioned about extensively by the Judges in respect to an earlier document. Have you discussed the question of the Joint Command with anyone in order for you to be able to give that long answer?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you I was the commander, and after the corps commander and Chief of Staff of the corps, the next line of command is the commanders of brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: May I repeat the question, with Your Honour's leave, so the witness can understand it. It's a very simple question, but I'm going to repeat it word-for-word: About 20 minutes ago you gave a very long answer about the Joint Command, something you'd been questioned about extensively by the Judges in respect to an earlier document. Have you discussed the question of the Joint Command with anyone in order for you to give that long answer that you gave about 20 minutes ago?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I discussed that also with my colleagues, commanders of other brigades.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Since you were giving evidence here? Since you answered the learned Judges about the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: So the long answer that you gave was simply a long answer you've always been able to give; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: BOZIDAR DELIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I've always been able to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: We'll compare it next week with the answers you gave earlier. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Robinson, could I be informed how long the cross-examination by Mr. Nice will take so that I can plan my schedule?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Nice?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICE
utterances.text: My considerable pleasure to do my best. As you know, I aim to take no more than 50 per cent of the time taken by the accused in evidence in chief, but I can't guarantee that. That would take me to the beginning of the week after next. It would, of course, be a matter for the accused and how long he takes with re-examination -- and I can't guarantee that, but assuming I were to finish at the beginning of the week after next, it would be a matter for him and his re-examination whether he can fit in another witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, that should be helpful to you.
